about: Named targets. ra, dec in degrees (ICRS) at `epoch` (stars, Pluto) or at `when` (the comet). A `fast` star also carries its catalogue astrometry: position and epoch, proper motion in mas/yr (pmra is the motion in RA times cos(dec)), parallax in mas, radial velocity in km/s.

entries.name: Barnard's Star

catalogue.source: Gaia DR3 4472832130942575872, ESA Gaia archive (gaiadr3.gaia_source), epoch J2016.0

entries.note: The fastest star in the sky: about 10.4 arcsec a year.

entries.name: Epsilon Indi B

catalogue.source: Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152, ESA Gaia archive (gaiadr3.gaia_source), epoch J2016.0

entries.note: A pair of brown dwarfs, Ba and Bb, about 0.4 degrees from Epsilon Indi A. Gaia lists the two as one source whose fit is poor (RUWE above 4): the position is that of the pair.

entries.name: WISE 0855-0714

catalogue.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7 (2021ApJS..253....7K), as served by SIMBAD for WISEA J085510.74-071442.5; the position is given at epoch J2000.0 there. Not in Gaia.
catalogue.unverified_why: Values read from SIMBAD; the paper itself was not opened and the epoch of the position was not read from it.

entries.note: The coldest brown dwarf known, about 8.1 arcsec a year. Not in Gaia.

entries.name: RW Aurigae

catalogue.source: Gaia DR3 156430822114424576, ESA Gaia archive (gaiadr3.gaia_source), epoch J2016.0

entries.note: A young star that dims irregularly. Gaia DR3 lists the two stars of the pair apart; this is the brighter, A.

entries.name: R Draconis

catalogue.source: Gaia DR3 1648328016354496384, ESA Gaia archive (gaiadr3.gaia_source), epoch J2016.0

entries.note: A pulsating red giant, bright and saturated in SPHEREx.

entries.name: Comet C/2025 A6 (Lemmon)
entries.source: JPL Horizons, astrometric ICRS position seen from SPHEREx, at 2026-02-26 20:41 UTC, between the two SPHEREx exposures of that night
entries.note: A moving target: this is its position on the night of 26 February 2026 only. It moves about 52 arcmin in 37.5 hours.

entries.name: Pluto
entries.source: JPL Horizons, astrometric ICRS position seen from SPHEREx, at 2026.0
entries.note: Moves slowly against the stars: about 0.04 arcsec an hour.
